item.title: What are soft tags? How do they differ from hard tags?
item.description:
In Model Training (especially model distillation) and Deep learning, Hard Targets/Labels and Soft Targets/Labels are two different ways to describe sample category information. Their core difference lies in the dimension of the information they contain and their impact on model training.

1. What is a hard label?

Hard labels are labels in the form of One-hot Encoding provided by the original dataset.

  • Manifestation: It only indicates the single correct category to which the sample belongs. For example, in a three-class classification task, if the sample belongs to the third class, its hard label is [0,0,1].
  • Information Content : The information is very singular. It can only tell the model “which category this sample belongs to” without providing any additional information about the correlation between categories.

2. What is a soft label?

Soft labels typically refer to the probability distribution output by a trained “teacher model”.

item.title: Ch1.1 What's RAG?
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are trained on large but fixed corpora, which limits their ability to reason about private or up-to-date information. Fine-tuning is a way to mitigate this issue, but it is generally not suitable for recalling factual information and is relatively costly. Against this backdrop, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has gradually emerged as a mainstream and powerful mechanism. RAG uses documents retrieved from external data sources as a Knowledge Base to enhance the generation capabilities of LLMs through in-context learning.

item.title: Ch1.2 IDE Configuration
item.description:
1.2 IDE Configuration

In Python development, there are two most commonly used Integrated Development Environments (IDEs): one is Jupyter Notebook, and the other is the well-known PyCharm. In this section, we will briefly introduce the usage methods of these two common development tools respectively.

1.2.1 Installation and Usage of Jupyter Notebook

Jupyter Notebook is a very powerful tool, especially in areas such as data science, scientific research, and presenting complex data analysis projects. Jupyter provides an interactive programming environment that allows us to write and run code, view results, modify code, and then run it again, making experimental analysis and data exploration very simple.Meanwhile, the Jupyter development page also has excellent support for data visualization tools (such as Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, etc.), making it easy to create interactive charts and visualizations. Additionally, Jupyter also supports writing relevant documentation in Markdown format on the development page.

item.title: About
item.description:
About Me

I am an AI engineer and have published three books in the field of AI so far. These include the simplified Chinese editions “「跟我一起学机器学习」” and “「跟我一起学深度学习」”, as well as the traditional Chinese edition “「一本書晉升深度學習世界級大師」”.

I have a deep understanding of the difficulties beginners face when entering the AI field, and I focus on helping newcomers quickly step through the door into the world of AI. The initial drafts of these materials originated from my study notes during my master’s program, including courses such as Andrew Ng’s Machine Learning course and Stanford University’s CS224N and CS231N. Since then, I have continuously refined and updated these materials for nearly 10 years.
